To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flow of non-newtonian shear-thinning fluids in a tube is not only influenced by the shear rate but also by the tube diameter, that the flow of shear-thinning fluids is more homogeneous than the flow of newtons fluids in the same geometry and that the flow of newtions fluids is more homogeneous in the case of a bundle of tubes than in the case of one tube.

the flow in the two-tube-system shows an interesting flow behavior, which can be described as a flow of two different fluids, one with the properties of the Newtonian fluid and the other with the properties of a shear-thinning fluid.
the flow of shear-thinning solutions through a bundle of tubes can be described by a simple model based on the flow through a single tube.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the flow behavior of non-Newtonian fluids in model filters by means of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and NMR spectroscopy.
the investigation of the flow of newtonsian and non-newtonian liquids in porous media by MRI.
the development and application of NMR-methods for the determination of rheological parameters and the investigation of the flow of newt. and non-newt. fluids in porous media.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flow of non-Newtonian fluids is more complicated than that of Newtonian fluids.

we were able to show that the flow of non-newtonian fluid can be described with a power law model and that there is a correlation between the flow behaviour of the fluid and the geometry of the tube bundle.
the NMR technique is a powerful tool to determine rheological properties of complex fluids in porous media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NMR method is a valuable tool for the investigation of the flow of non-newtonian and newtonian fluids through porous media.
the flow of shear-thinning fluids in a single tube can be described as the flow of a newtonian fluid of the same viscosity as the shear-thinning fluid at a characteristic shear rate.

the flow of non-newtonian fluid through a bundle of tubes or a packing of beads can be described by the same equations as that through single tubes or two-tube-system, if the effective diameter of the tubes is defined by the mean diameter of the pores.
